questions.title: Correct statement about vitamin D
questions.question: Which one of the following statements concerning vitamin D is correct?

options.A: Chronic renal failure requires the oral administration of 1-alpha hydroxycholecalciferol
options.B: It is required in the diet of individuals exposed to sunlight
options.C: 25-Hydroxycholecalciferol is the active form of the vitamin
options.D: Vitamin D opposes the effect of parathyroid hormone
options.E: A deficiency in vitamin D results in an increased secretion of calcitonin

explanations.A: Correct. Chronic renal failure destroys the kidney's own 1-alpha-hydroxylase capacity, so plain vitamin D or even 25-hydroxyvitamin D cannot be activated; the patient must be given 1-alpha-hydroxycholecalciferol (or calcitriol itself), a preparation that bypasses the missing renal step. This is the standard treatment for renal osteodystrophy. Without it, calcium absorption and bone mineralisation stay impaired despite normal vitamin D intake.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Adequate sunlight exposure lets skin synthesise sufficient vitamin D on its own (via UV conversion of 7-dehydrocholesterol), so dietary vitamin D is not strictly required in a sun-exposed individual.
explanations.C: Incorrect. 25-hydroxycholecalciferol is the main circulating storage form, not the active hormone -- the active form is 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D (calcitriol), made by the kidney's second hydroxylation step.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Vitamin D (as calcitriol) works together with parathyroid hormone, not against it -- both raise serum calcium, and PTH itself stimulates the renal 1-alpha-hydroxylase step that activates vitamin D.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Vitamin D deficiency lowers serum calcium, which triggers a rise in parathyroid hormone (secondary hyperparathyroidism), not an increase in calcitonin, which is instead released when calcium rises.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the single correct statement about vitamin D among several plausible-sounding distractors, centred on renal failure's need for an already-activated preparation.

questions.title: Vitamin D preparation for resistant rickets
questions.question: Which Vitamin D preparation is recommended for a patient with Vitamin D resistant rickets?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Plain vitamin D3 still requires two intact hydroxylation steps (liver 25-hydroxylase, then renal 1-alpha-hydroxylase) to become active; in vitamin-D-resistant rickets the renal step is the one that is missing.
explanations.B: Incorrect. 24,25-dihydroxyvitamin D3 is an inactive metabolite, not a therapeutic activation product.
explanations.C: Correct. Vitamin-D-resistant rickets (vitamin-D-dependent rickets type I) results from a genetic deficiency of renal 1-alpha-hydroxylase, so treatment must supply a preparation that is already 1-alpha-hydroxylated -- 1-hydroxy D3 (or calcitriol) -- bypassing the missing enzyme entirely. The same 1-alpha-hydroxylated logic applies to the chronic-renal-failure scenario in the preceding question.
explanations.D: Incorrect. 25-hydroxy D3 still requires the missing 1-alpha-hydroxylase step to become fully active, so it does not correct the defect.
explanations.E: Incorrect. 1,24,25-trihydroxy D3 is a further, minor hydroxylated metabolite, not the standard therapeutic preparation for this condition.

questions.learning_objective: Name a 1-alpha-hydroxylated vitamin D preparation as the correct treatment for 1-alpha-hydroxylase-deficient vitamin-D-resistant rickets.

questions.title: Vitamin required for intestinal calcium absorption
questions.question: Which vitamin is required for calcium absorption from the small intestine?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Vitamin A's roles are in vision and epithelial differentiation, not intestinal calcium transport.
explanations.B: Correct. Calcitriol (1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D), the active hormone made by sequential liver and kidney hydroxylation of vitamin D, acts on intestinal epithelial cells to increase synthesis of calcium-binding proteins (e.g. calbindin) and calcium channels, directly raising active calcium absorption from the small intestine.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Vitamin E is primarily an antioxidant and has no established direct role in intestinal calcium absorption.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Vitamin K is a cofactor for gamma-carboxylation of clotting factors and some bone matrix proteins (e.g. osteocalcin), not a driver of intestinal calcium absorption.

questions.learning_objective: Name vitamin D (as calcitriol) as the vitamin required for intestinal calcium absorption.

questions.title: Parathyroid hormone actions -- which is false
questions.question: All of the following are true about Parathyroid hormone actions, EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Incorrect (i.e. this is true). Raising serum calcium is PTH's defining overall effect, achieved via its actions on bone, kidney and (indirectly) intestine.
explanations.B: Incorrect (i.e. this is true). PTH increases renal tubular calcium reabsorption, directly conserving calcium that would otherwise be filtered and lost in urine.
explanations.C: Incorrect (i.e. this is true). PTH stimulates renal 1-alpha-hydroxylase, increasing calcitriol production, which further raises calcium via enhanced intestinal absorption.
explanations.D: Correct as the exception. PTH actually decreases renal phosphate reabsorption (it is phosphaturic), promoting phosphate excretion in urine -- the opposite of what this option claims -- while simultaneously raising calcium, which is why PTH is said to lower the calcium-phosphate product in the kidney's handling of the two ions. Recognising this phosphaturic effect is what separates a complete list of PTH's actions from an incomplete one.

questions.learning_objective: State PTH's four classic actions and identify that it decreases (not increases) renal phosphate reabsorption.

questions.title: Calcitonin actions -- which is false
questions.question: All of the following are true about Calcitonin hormone actions, EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Incorrect (i.e. this is true). Lowering serum calcium is calcitonin's defining overall effect.
explanations.B: Incorrect (i.e. this is true). Calcitonin decreases renal tubular calcium reabsorption, promoting calcium loss in urine and thereby lowering serum calcium.
explanations.C: Correct as the exception. Calcitonin actually inhibits osteoclast activity (suppressing bone resorption), which is precisely how it lowers serum calcium -- the option's claim that it 'activates' osteoclast activity is the reverse of its true action. This inhibitory action is the direct mechanistic basis for calcitonin's calcium-lowering effect.
explanations.D: Incorrect (i.e. this is true). Calcitonin increases phosphate excretion in urine, consistent with its general calcium- and phosphate-lowering effect.

questions.learning_objective: State calcitonin's actions and identify that it inhibits (not activates) osteoclast bone resorption.

questions.title: Correct calcium body distribution
questions.question: Which of the following represents a correct calcium distribution?

options.A: It represents 0.1% of total body weight
options.B: 1.5% of calcium is stored in bones
options.C: 99% of calcium is present in soft tissues
options.D: 0.1% of calcium is present in plasma
options.E: 0.1% of calcium is present in teeth

explanations.A: Incorrect. Calcium is actually a larger share of total body weight than 0.1% (roughly 1-2%), reflecting how much of it is locked into the skeleton.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Far more than 1.5% of body calcium is stored in bone -- about 99% of the total body calcium pool is skeletal.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Soft tissue holds only a small slice of total body calcium, not 99% -- 99% is bone, and soft tissue/extracellular fluid/plasma together make up only about 1%.
explanations.D: Correct. Plasma calcium is a very small fraction, roughly 0.1% of total body calcium, held within a narrow, tightly regulated range despite the enormous skeletal reservoir sitting alongside it -- this small fraction is exactly what the PTH-calcitriol-calcitonin loop is constantly adjusting. Recognising this heavy skeletal skew is essential to understanding why even small percentage shifts in bone turnover can noticeably move plasma calcium.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Teeth contain a meaningful mineral reserve as part of the skeletal/dental calcium pool, but this specific figure does not represent the correct distribution.

questions.learning_objective: State that roughly 99% of body calcium is skeletal and only about 0.1% circulates in plasma.

questions.title: Fat-soluble vitamin
questions.question: Which of the following vitamins is fat-soluble?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Vitamin C is water-soluble, absorbed and excreted along with the body's water compartment rather than stored in fat.
explanations.B: Correct. Vitamin D belongs to the fat-soluble vitamin group (A, D, E, K), which is why it is absorbed with dietary fat, transported on lipoproteins, and can be stored in adipose tissue and liver -- unlike the water-soluble B and C vitamins. This fat-solubility is also why vitamin D toxicity (unlike water-soluble vitamin excess) can accumulate to harmful levels with excessive supplementation.

questions.learning_objective: Classify vitamin D as fat-soluble, alongside A, E and K.

questions.title: Where D3 is present -- the exception
questions.question: D3 (cholecalciferol) is present in all of the following, EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Correct as the exception. Skin does not contain preformed vitamin D3 -- it holds the inactive precursor 7-dehydrocholesterol, which UV radiation converts photochemically to previtamin D3 and then D3. Because what is actually present under the skin is the precursor rather than the finished molecule, 'under the skin' is the odd one out when the question asks where D3 itself is present.
explanations.B: Incorrect (i.e. D3 is present here). Cod liver oil is one of the richest classic dietary sources of preformed vitamin D3.
explanations.C: Incorrect (i.e. D3 is present here). Fatty (oily) fish such as salmon and mackerel are well-known dietary sources of preformed vitamin D3.
explanations.D: Incorrect (i.e. D3 is present here). Egg yolk contains a meaningful amount of preformed vitamin D3.
explanations.E: Incorrect (i.e. D3 is present here, per the source paper's own answer key). Beef liver is grouped with the other listed animal-derived foods as a dietary source of preformed D3 on this exam.

questions.learning_objective: Distinguish dietary sources that contain preformed vitamin D3 from skin, which holds only its precursor until UV conversion.

questions.title: Order of calcitriol's mechanism steps
questions.question: Arrange the following steps in the mechanism of calcitriol: 1) Binding a nuclear receptor; 2) Increase intestinal absorption of calcium; 3) Binding to a specific DNA sequence; 4) Activates transcription; 5) Calbindin synthesis. Which is the correct order?

explanations.A: Correct. As a steroid-family hormone, calcitriol first binds its nuclear receptor (1), the receptor-hormone complex then binds a specific DNA sequence (a vitamin D response element) (3), this activates transcription of target genes (4), one of which is calbindin, a calcium-binding protein whose synthesis follows (5), and the resulting calbindin increases intestinal calcium absorption (2), the hormone's overall physiological effect. Getting this receptor-then-DNA-then-transcription order right reflects the same general mechanism shared by other steroid/nuclear-receptor hormones.
explanations.B: Incorrect. This places calcium absorption (2) before calbindin synthesis (5), but calbindin must first be made from the transcribed gene before it can do the work of increasing calcium absorption.
explanations.C: Incorrect. This places DNA-sequence binding (3) after transcriptional activation (4), but the receptor must bind its specific DNA response element before it can activate transcription of the target gene.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Like option C, this reverses DNA binding and transcriptional activation, and it also places calcium absorption before calbindin synthesis, getting two steps out of order.

questions.learning_objective: Sequence calcitriol's nuclear-receptor mechanism from receptor binding through to increased intestinal calcium absorption.

questions.title: Hormone acting at high-normal calcium
questions.question: Which of the following hormones is acting when calcium level is 11 mg/dL?

explanations.A: Incorrect. PTH is secreted in response to a falling (low) calcium, not a high-normal value like 11 mg/dL.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Calcitriol production is driven upstream by PTH's response to low calcium; it is not the hormone whose secretion is triggered by a high-normal calcium value.
explanations.C: Correct. At 11 mg/dL, calcium sits at the upper end of (or just above) the normal range, which is exactly the stimulus that triggers calcitonin release from thyroid parafollicular cells -- calcitonin acts to bring an elevated calcium back down by suppressing osteoclastic bone resorption. Recognising which direction calcium is moving is the key to picking the right hormone in this kind of numeric vignette.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Both PTH and calcitriol are the hormones mobilised by low calcium, the opposite scenario to the high-normal value given here.

questions.learning_objective: Apply the calcium-homeostasis loop to a high-normal calcium value, identifying calcitonin as the active hormone.

questions.title: Hormone acting at low calcium
questions.question: Which of the following hormones is acting when calcium level is 7 mg/dL?

explanations.A: Incorrect alone. PTH is indeed released at a low calcium such as 7 mg/dL, but calcitriol production is also driven up in parallel (PTH itself stimulates renal 1-alpha-hydroxylase), so PTH alone is an incomplete answer.
explanations.B: Incorrect alone. Calcitriol is likewise mobilised at low calcium (via PTH-stimulated renal activation), but naming calcitriol alone omits PTH's own direct actions.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Calcitonin is released in response to a rising, not a falling, calcium -- it would not be the active hormone at a low value like 7 mg/dL.
explanations.D: Correct. A low calcium of 7 mg/dL triggers PTH release, and PTH in turn stimulates renal 1-alpha-hydroxylase to raise calcitriol production -- both hormones act together in this scenario, PTH directly on bone and kidney, and calcitriol on the intestine, to restore serum calcium. Recognising that both hormones act together, not just one, is the key distinction this question tests.

questions.learning_objective: Apply the calcium-homeostasis loop to a low calcium value, identifying that both PTH and calcitriol act together.
